name: Susisuchus
isnote: PBDB lists Susisuchus under Eusuchia, and White et al. (2022) place the susisuchids with the hylaeochampsids inside it, whereas Salisbury et al. (2006) placed Susisuchus outside Eusuchia as its sister taxon; it is therefore kept in Neosuchia, the deepest group they share.
sum: Early Cretaceous crocodyliform from the Crato Formation of Brazil with a segmented back shield like that of eusuchians but simple vertebrae.
wsnote: The sources give no body length; Salisbury et al. (2003), as summarised on Wikipedia, argue that the high-walking posture would have kept it below about 50 kg.
holotype: Partial articulated skeleton of S. anatoceps with skull, lower jaw, forelimbs, parts of the axial skeleton and osteoderms — Crato Formation (Nova Olinda Member), Araripe Basin, Brazil (Salisbury et al. 2003).
material: The holotype is the most complete specimen. S. jaguaribensis (2009) rests on fragmentary remains from the Lima Campos Basin, about 115 km away; a further limb specimen from the Crato Formation was tentatively assigned as cf. Susisuchus.
exceptional: Traces of soft tissue around both forelimbs and the digits of the right hand; the carcass is thought to have dried out before burial.
biology: Susisuchus was among the first mesoeucrocodylians with a tetraserial paravertebral shield, four rows of osteoderms along the back, which gave the trunk more lateral flexibility for swimming while keeping it rigid enough for semi-erect walking. It kept amphicoelous (concave-ended) vertebrae, a primitive trait, so it is regarded as a transitional form. Salisbury et al. argued that high-walking limited its size.
author: Salisbury et al. 2003

sources.text: Salisbury, S.W. 2003. A new crocodilian from the Lower Cretaceous Crato Formation of north-eastern Brazil. Palaeontographica Abteilung A 270(1–3): 3–47. doi:10.1127/pala/270/2003/3
